title: Cybersickness from vestibular-visual mismatch
bottleneck: When the eyes report motion that the inner ear doesn't feel (or vice versa), the sensory conflict triggers nausea, dizziness, and disorientation in a large fraction of users. Artificial locomotion via thumbstick is the worst offender, and dropped frames or reprojection artifacts amplify it. Comfort settings (vignetting, teleportation) reduce sickness only by reducing immersion.
why_it_blocks: Cybersickness is the single biggest adoption barrier for VR: a substantial share of the population can't use it comfortably at all. Every application requiring virtual movement must choose between comfort and presence.
current_state: Higher refresh rates, lower latency, and inside-out tracking have reduced but not eliminated sickness; susceptibility varies widely and 'VR legs' don't develop for everyone. No universal countermeasure exists. Susceptibility varies widely between individuals, so no single comfort preset works for the whole population.
